description: What a sandboxed execution worker can signal, and whether its descendants can leave its process group. The source is tests/shared/sandbox-signals.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

cases.description: Each runner starts the victim, then sends a case's `code` for its own language to a fresh sandboxed worker, after replacing `{host_pid}` and `{host_group}` with the pid and process group of the process that started the worker, and `{sigurg}` with SIGURG's number on the host. It compares the tool result, with surrounding whitespace removed, against `output`, then stops the victim and checks that it heard nothing. R's `tools::pskill()` ignores a pid that is not positive, so the R code signals a process group through the shell's `kill`, and closes the shell's stderr rather than redirecting it, since the worker cannot write to `/dev/null` under Landlock. SIGURG is the signal sent outside the worker because its default action is to ignore it, so a sandbox that fails a case leaves the host and the user's other processes running. A case listing `platforms` runs only where `platform.system()` or `Sys.info()[["sysname"]]`, lowercased, is one of them: seatbelt has no rule for process groups, so on macOS a descendant can still start a session of its own. Runners skip every case on a host that cannot sandbox the worker.
cases.victim: trap 'echo received' URG; while :; do sleep 0.1; done

cases.name: the host's process group cannot be signalled

code.r: cat(system('kill -s URG -- -{host_group} 2>&-; s=$?; case $s in 0) echo delivered;; 1) echo refused;; *) echo status $s;; esac', intern = TRUE))

cases.name: a signal to every process reaches nothing outside the worker
the worker can signal its own child

code.r:
job <- parallel::mcparallel(Sys.sleep(30))
sent <- tools::pskill(job$pid, tools::SIGTERM)
invisible(suppressWarnings(parallel::mccollect(job)))
cat(if (sent) 'delivered' else 'refused')
code.python:
import subprocess, sys
child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(30)'])
child.terminate()
print('delivered' if child.wait() == -15 else 'refused')

cases.name: a child cannot start a session of its own

code.r: cat(system('setsid true 2>&-; s=$?; case $s in 0) echo allowed;; 1) echo refused;; *) echo status $s;; esac', intern = TRUE))
